newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent up as Venezuela's Maracaibo blocked.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent up as Venezuela's Maracaibo blocked.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures hit intra-days highs on Tuesday afternoon, helped by news that Venezuela's main oil export shipping channel had been blocked.
October Brent was up 13 cents a barrel at $19.06 at 1415 GMT, having hit an intra-day high of $19.10 a few minutes earlier.
"The Maracaibo news helped lift prices," said Leslie Nicholas at brokers GNI in London.
A dredger went aground in the Lake Maracaibo shipping lane on Monday night, shutting the channel to tankers which normally export more than one million barrels of crude per day.
"Nothing is coming in and nothing is going out," said a shipping agent on Tuesday.
Adding upward pressure to the market was a big jump on NYMEX gasoline which been highly volatile in recent days.
September NYMEX gasoline was up over one cent a gallon in early trading, boosting European gasoline which in turn lifted Brent futures.
Resistance on Brent was pegged by analysts at $19.29, the high from last Thursday and at $19.46 from a downtrend line joining the highs of May 16 and August 4.
Gas oil also gained. September was up $1.75 a tonne at $171.25 at 1411 GMT despite a sluggish physical market.
Stocks of winter heating oil are well above year ago levels on both sides of the Atlantic and sellers are having to work harder than buyers to drum up interest.
Prompt Rotterdam barges are at parity to the IPE, as are cargoes of Russian gas oil heading for Western buyers.
